name: Wilderness Drive Campground
note: Drayton Park Board campground on the north edge of town between ND 44 and I-29: sites along gravel lanes between shelterbelt tree rows. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: City of Drayton Park Facilities page (draytonnd.com/park-facilities, read 2026-11-12): 'Wilderness Drive Campground ... 250 Wilderness Drive ... 70 Full-Hookup sites, 10 Primitive sites, Water, Sewer, 50-amp Electrical, Wi-Fi, Picnic tables and fire rings at each site, Hot Showers, Flush Toilets', 'north of Drayton ... At the 4-way stop, go north on Hwy 44 approx. 1 mile. Campground is on your left', 'CLOSED to the public for the months of September and October of each year, as it becomes temporary home to hundreds of sugarbeet harvest workers. Please try one of our other campgrounds', '2026 Rates: Nightly $35.00 Weekly $175.00 Monthly $400.00', contact 701-520-1926, map pin D at 48.578533,-97.180930; city sheet 2024_Drayton_Campgrounds.pdf (draytonnd.com/documents/543, read 2026-11-12): 'Wilderness RV Park - (70 units) ... Has Water/Sewer hookups, 30 and 50 AMP, modern restrooms and showers', '**Owned and operated by the Drayton Park Board**'; ND HHS Statewide Licensed RV Parks/Campgrounds (updated 07.17.2025) row 425: WILDERNESS CAMPGROUND, Highway 44 & 66, owner DRAYTON PARK DISTRICT, 70 lots -> a park-district campground selling single nights (local: no price gate or presence rule). Separate from 15687 Drayton RV Park (0.94 km S, own city-page section, HHS row 97) and 6049 Schumacher Park (1.4 km, HHS row 98). Workforce test: the crews hold it only in September and October; the rest of the season it is open to the public, and The Dyrt camper review (Teresa T., May 2024): 'a sizable campground for people who work on the sugar beet in the fall but available the rest of the year ... very few permanent campers here right now'; Esri summer imagery 2026-11-12 shows ~12 rigs in ~70 sites -> not mainly a workforce park, and long-stay test 4 passes (no count published; the evidence points to a mostly nightly public season, so no long-term caveat). Esri imagery (z19-equivalent, 320 m frame at 48.5772,-97.1830): wide gravel lanes between tree rows with rigs parked alongside, 30-40-ft trailers present -> a 23-ft rig fits. No horse facilities, no road warning (paved ND 44, I-29 exit 187).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-12: Esri World Imagery (3 km frame at 48.5785,-97.175; 800 m and 320 m frames at the campground): the campground sits in farmland north of Drayton between I-29 and ND 44/the railroad; the nearest water is a Red River oxbow ~1.2 km east beyond ND 44, the railroad and crop fields, out of sight of every site. The only nearer water is the sugar factory's industrial settling ponds ~0.6 km north (not a water value). No site is near any water -> not waterfront.
fees_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities ('Wilderness Drive Campground ... 2026 Rates: Nightly $35.00 Weekly $175.00 Monthly $400.00 U.S. Funds only'), read 2026-11-12. Third-party $20-25 (The Dyrt, Campendium) is stale.
hookups_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities ('70 Full-Hookup sites', 'Water', 'Sewer', '50-amp Electrical') and 2024_Drayton_Campgrounds.pdf ('Water/Sewer hookups, 30 and 50 AMP'), read 2026-11-12
sites_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities ('70 Full-Hookup sites', '10 Primitive sites'); 2024 city sheet (70 units); ND HHS list 07.17.2025 (70 lots), read 2026-11-12
facilities_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities ('Wi-Fi', 'Hot Showers', 'Flush Toilets') and 2024 city sheet ('modern restrooms and showers'), read 2026-11-12

season.note: Closed to the public every September and October, when it houses the sugar-beet harvest crews.

season_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities ('CLOSED to the public for the months of September and October of each year, as it becomes temporary home to hundreds of sugarbeet harvest workers'), read 2026-11-12. Opening and closing dates for the rest of the year are not published.
booking_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities (contact 701-520-1926; no online booking) and The Dyrt camper review May 2024 ('you need to call the phone number to get a spot'), read 2026-11-12
status_source: https://draytonnd.com/park-facilities (2026 rates posted, Sep-Oct crew closure described as an annual arrangement, not a closure), read 2026-11-12; The Dyrt review dated 2026-10-23 from a beet-harvest stay
flags: Name: the city page calls it Wilderness Drive Campground; its own 2024 sheet says 'Wilderness RV Park' and HHS 'Wilderness Campground'. RV Life 'Drayton RV Campground' (254023, no reviews), Campendium 'Drayton RV Park' (250 Wilderness Dr) and The Dyrt 'Drayton Campground' (pin 48.5757,-97.1833) all describe this park; RV Life has no rating, so no rvlife value.
Pin moved ~210 m SW from the city's map pin (on Wilderness Dr at the bathhouse entrance) to the centre of the site lanes.
Season: only the Sep-Oct crew closure is published; whether it is open in winter is unknown, so no opens/closes written.
Booking: platform phone from the city contact plus a 2024 camper review; reservable left unwritten (no stated reservation policy).
curation_note: ND lead 11 (2026-11-12): also published as 'Wilderness RV Park' (city 2024 sheet) and 'Wilderness Campground' (HHS row 425); third-party listings carry it as RV Life 'Drayton RV Campground' (254023), Campendium 'Drayton RV Park' (250 Wilderness Dr), The Dyrt 'Drayton Campground' and Google 'Drayton RV Park'. The city's name is followed. Workforce test: crews only Sep-Oct; a May 2024 camper saw very few permanent campers; summer imagery ~12 rigs in ~70 sites -> passes, no long-term caveat.
